title: The Memory Sinkhole - Unleashing An X86 Design Flaw Allowing Universal Privilege Escalation
summary: Christopher Domas's Black Hat 2015 talk on a long-unnoticed x86 design flaw that lets an attacker reach System Management Mode, a ring below the OS. It explains how the legacy architecture allows universal privilege escalation and persistent, hard-to-detect malware.
why: Cited in discussions of CPU hidden features, Intel's security failures and SMM malware as a concrete example of a forgotten processor feature being exploited.

quote.text: There was a blackhat talk on embedding malware in SMM and triggering it with a magic number written to a register
